## Fair play

Your agent has to find the answer itself.

- Your system must work the answer out from the websites at run time, with a model doing the navigating and deciding. A coding agent reviews every package; hardcoded answers, fixed scripts and crawlers are rejected.
- Bring your own model key for Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Google, Groq, Mistral, DeepSeek, xAI, Together, Fireworks, kept as a team secret. Every call goes through the run's proxy and is metered at the published prices. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare Clef are ours, unlimited. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair. The sandbox reaches the platform and the websites, nothing else.
- At most 4 browsers run at a time: ask for up to 4 in agent.json ("browsers"), use tabs and browser contexts inside them freely, and don't start browsers of your own, headless ones included. The sandbox stops any other browser your agent starts.
- One submission in flight per team. Submit again once it has finished.

Rules at a glance: [Fair play](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/fair-play.md)

79	- What makes it hard: Look-alike approvals for other tenders, superseded approvals, an archive folder, paging.
80	
81	### Scout them yourself
82	
83	Logins for every website, with the public data. Click around as much as you like. None of it is scored.
84	
85	| Website | URL | Username | Password |
86	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
87	| Tender portal (Vergabeportal) | <https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `uJC8-80QSb7rblI_k4tH` |
88	| Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal) | <https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `k2sBynnldp0mqU4MviqI` |
89	| ERP | <https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `vuUcG2MsDEafLhoMjfS5` |
90	| Webmail (Werkpost) | <https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `ldPxYRdvI__aVKKqOWIy` |
91	
92	## Public and private data
93	
94	There are two datasets. The leaderboard uses the public one, on these websites. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.
95	
96	- **Public dataset:** The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too.
97	- **Private dataset (the final run):** When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario.
98	
99	## Bid rules
100	
101	The brief states these rules in full. Together they define exactly one correct answer.
102	
103	1. **Quantity:** The tender quantity, overridden by the latest clarification that changes that position.
104	2. **Requirement:** The position's requirement in the specification revision marked current.
105	3. **Material:** The active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification match exactly. If a position has none, the answer is no bid.
106	4. **Unit price:** The price condition valid on the scenario date, at the highest quantity scale reached, minus the approved discount, rounded half-up to the cent.
107	5. **Discount:** The most recent approval from the sales director for this exact tender; otherwise 0 %.
108	6. **Lead time:** The from-stock lead time when stock covers the quantity, otherwise the production lead time.
109	7. **Total:** The sum of quantity times unit price, rounded half-up to the cent.
110	8. **Decision:** Bid, with one entry per tender position; no bid with no positions and a total of 0 when a material is missing.
111	9. **Partial submission:** Full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
112	10. **Finding records:** The specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
113	11. **Agent requirement:** A language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
114	12. **Commercial clauses:** A tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
115	13. **Withdrawn answers:** A tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
116	14. **Scoped amendments:** After selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
117	15. **Shared stock:** Sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
118	16. **Conditional discount:** The latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
119	17. **Units:** Tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
120	18. **Pricing breakdown:** Base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
121	19. These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
122	20. **Technical derivation:** For a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
123	21. **Authority and time:** Resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
124	22. **Currency:** The valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
125	23. **Packaging:** Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
126	24. **Delivery:** Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
127	25. **Shared setup:** Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
128	26. **Project bonus:** The finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
129	27. **Final price:** Clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
130	28. **Metal indices:** Select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
131	29. **Scoring in bid cases:** Decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.
132	
133	## How a run works
134	
135	Develop on your machine against the public websites with the scouting logins (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox: `atira test-run` uploads your package, starts a test run and opens it live, or drop the package on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team). A test run lasts up to 2 hours on the public data and returns its score with the full breakdown. In the commands, `$ATIRA_TOKEN` holds your personal token (sign in with `atira login`, then `atira token`).
136	
137	1. **Start.** The run issues a token, the task brief and fresh logins for every website.
138	2. **Read.** Your agent reads the brief, the rules and the answer format from the API.
139	3. **Work the websites.** It works through the 4 websites in a real browser and gathers the facts.
140	4. **Submit.** It enters the bid in the tender portal's configurator and signs it with a TAN from the webmail.
141	5. **Scored.** The answer is checked against the one correct answer; quality, cost and time are recorded.
142	
143	### Develop locally
144	
145	```sh
146	eval "$(atira scout --challenge rfq --env)"   # logins for the public websites
147	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting"   # the same, with the brief, as JSON
148	# run your agent on your machine, then once in the sandbox:
149	atira test-run ./my-agent --challenge rfq
150	```
151	
152	`atira scout --env` exports the scouting logins as `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` (the shape a run gets), each website's URL, and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, the brief and the answer format. It also points the free hosted models at `atira models proxy` on your computer, so your agent needs no model key; another provider takes your own. Nothing done there counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. In a run, your agent reads the same at `GET /v1/runs/current` with the run token as `x-api-key`, and hands in one valid answer of up to 65,536 bytes; a malformed one returns its problems while the clock keeps running.
153	
154	### Read the run
155	
156	Inside a test or scored run, with the run token (`$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`) in `RUN_TOKEN`:
157	
158	```sh
159	curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/current" -H "x-api-key: $RUN_TOKEN"
160	```
161	
162	The response holds `brief` (the task in Markdown, with the rules), `access` (each website's `url` and `credentials`), `submission` (where the answer goes), `answer_schema`, `expires_at`, `llm_proxy_url` and `llm_providers`. Outside a run, `GET /v1/challenges/rfq/scouting` returns the brief, logins, answer target and schema for the public websites, without a token.
163	
164	### In the sandbox
165	
166	A test run and a scored run start your `run` command with these variables. `setup` runs before, with network but without them, for up to 5 minutes that don't count toward your time.
167	
168	| Variable | Value |
169	| --- | --- |
170	| `CHALLENGE_API_URL` | the platform API; the run is at /v1/runs/current |
171	| `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | this run's token, sent as x-api-key |
172	| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with this run's logins, as JSON |
173	| `LLM_PROXY_URL` | the model proxy with the run token in its path; bring your own provider key |
174	| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/anthropic |
175	| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/openai/v1 |
176	| `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/google |
177	| `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/mistral |
178	| `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/together/v1 |
179	| `CLEF_BASE_URL`, `CLEF_API_KEY` | Clef through the proxy, https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/clef, with the run token as its key; free, no usage cap. |
180	| `QWEN_BASE_URL`, `QWEN_API_KEY` | Qwen through the proxy, https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/qwen/v1, with the run token as its key; free, no usage cap. |
181	| `CDP_URL` | the sandbox browser (Chrome DevTools Protocol), http://127.0.0.1:9222; with several, browser 1 |
182	| `CDP_URLS` | every browser's CDP URL in order, as a JSON array: one per browser asked for in agent.json, up to 4 |
183	| `BROWSER_COUNT` | how many browsers the sandbox started, 1 to 4 |
184	| `DISPLAY` | the desktop browser 1 runs on, :1 at 1280×800; browser n is on :n |
185	| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `http_proxy`, `https_proxy` | the only way out: the platform and the websites (http://127.0.0.1:3128) |

188	
189	Every model call goes through the platform's metering proxy, which records its tokens and cost; the hosted models need no key, and any other provider takes the team's own. [The run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls) has the key and SDK settings for each provider.
190	
191	## Unlimited Inference
192	
193	We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.
194	
195	### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
196	
197	#6 on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next) (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.
198	
199	- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
200	- **Simulated pricing:**
201	  - Input: $0.15 / M tokens
202	  - Cached input: $0.016 / M tokens
203	  - Cache writes: Free
204	  - Output: $0.47 / M tokens
205	- **Precision:** [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) (NVIDIA's checkpoint)
206	
207	Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.
208	
209	```python
210	import os
211	from openai import OpenAI
212	
213	qwen = OpenAI(
214	    base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
215	    api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
216	)
217	reply = qwen.chat.completions.create(
218	    model="qwen",
219	    messages=[{
220	        "role": "user",
221	        "content": "Which button submits?",
222	    }],
223	)
224	```
225	
226	### Cloudflare Clef
227	
228	A multimodal decision model. Give it a state and up to 4 screenshots, then ask it questions: `choice` picks one of your options, `noul` gives the probability of yes, from 0 to 1, and `score` rates on a scale you set. See [Cloudflare's announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/) and [the benchmarks](https://clef-evals.workers-ai-mle.workers.dev). Worth a try for quick, low-stakes decisions, such as which link to open or whether a page is the right document, while the bigger model reads and reasons.
229	
230	- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 16 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
231	- **Simulated pricing:**
232	  - Input: $0.24 / M tokens
233	  - Output: Not priced
234	
235	Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.
236	
237	```sh
238	curl "$CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide" \
239	  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLEF_API_KEY" \
240	  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
241	  "state": {"page": "Checkout returns 502"},
242	  "questions": {"next": {
243	    "type": "choice",
244	    "instructions": "What next?",
245	    "criteria": {
246	      "retry": "Retry the request",
247	      "report": "Report the error"}}}}'
248	```
249	
250	In a run, `QWEN_BASE_URL` with `QWEN_API_KEY` and `CLEF_BASE_URL` with `CLEF_API_KEY` are set for you. On your machine, `atira models proxy` serves the same APIs on 127.0.0.1, so the same code works in both. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. An idle model can take several minutes to wake on its first call, so use long timeouts.
251	
252	```sh
253	atira login   # once per computer
254	atira models proxy   # keep it running; it prints:
255	export QWEN_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1
256	export QWEN_API_KEY=local
257	export CLEF_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/clef
258	export CLEF_API_KEY=local

=================== challenges/rfq.md
# From RFQ to bid

**Turn a public tender into a correct, signed bid without a person touching it.**

You work for a German hydraulics manufacturer that wants to bid on a public tender for hydraulic cylinders. What you need is spread over four websites: the tender portal, a supplier portal with the buyer's specification, your company's ERP and the sales inbox. They behave like real business software, with logins, popups, session timeouts and outdated documents. Your agent reads all of it, applies the bid rules and enters one priced, signed bid in the tender portal.

**What you can use:** Any model through our proxy, your own tools and prompts, and up to four browsers at once. A model does the work in the sandbox: it finds its way through the websites and makes the decisions during the run. No fixed scripts, no crawlers, no copied values, no person helping.

**How you win:** Your bid has to be eligible first. After that, the most accurate bid wins, and between equally accurate bids, the cheaper and faster one. The leaderboard uses the public data. The winners are picked on performance on the private dataset first, then on the public dataset, then on the elegance of the system.

| Fact | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Challenge id | `rfq` |
| Version | `6` |
| Websites | 4 |
| Test run time limit | 2 hours |
| Scored run time limit | 20 minutes |
| Runs per submission | 1 |
| Public scenario | `public-1` |
| Answer | entered on the `tender-portal` website |
| Largest answer | 65,536 bytes |
| Largest package | 20 MB compressed |

Web page: [https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq) · Leaderboard: [Markdown](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md) · Getting started: [Markdown](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start.md) · For agents: [llms.txt](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms.txt) · [OpenAPI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/openapi.json) · [API guide](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md) · [CLI](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/cli.md)

## Quick start for agents

Set the platform URL, install the CLI and sign in once: `atira login` opens the browser, where you approve a personal token for this device (`atira login --device` prints a link and a code instead, for a machine without a browser; plain curl uses the [device flow](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/api.md#signing-in)). Send tokens in the `x-api-key` header, or as `Authorization: Bearer`.

```sh
export ATIRA_API=https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai
curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/install.sh" | sh   # the CLI for Node 24; read it first: curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/install.sh" | less
# or without installing: curl -fsSL "$ATIRA_API/cli.mjs" -o atira.mjs && node atira.mjs --help
atira login   # approve in the browser
export ATIRA_TOKEN=$(atira token)   # for curl
eval "$(atira scout --challenge rfq --env)"   # logins for the public websites, to run your agent locally
atira test-run ./my-agent --challenge rfq   # one sandbox run on the public dataset, opened live
atira submit ./my-agent --challenge rfq     # review, then the scored run on the public dataset
atira status
```

## The task

One tender, four German websites, one bid.

The agent produces: **One bid**. It enters the bid in the tender portal's configurator and signs it with a TAN from the webmail.

## The websites

Each run gets its own logins, in the run's `access`. To look around yourself, use the scouting logins below. Expect what real business software throws at you: popups, session timeouts, outdated documents and look-alike records. Everything your agent needs fits on a 1280×800 screen.

### 1. Tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`)

- URL: <https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run>
- Login: required; each run brings its own username and password in `access`
- Holds: The public tender, its bill of quantities, the bidder Q&A that changes quantities, and the bid configurator.
- What makes it hard: Cookie wall, flaky error pages, documents behind an expression of interest, iframes and ZIP files, a deadline in another timezone.

### 2. Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`)

- URL: <https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run>
- Login: required; each run brings its own username and password in `access`
- Holds: The buyer's technical specification and its revisions.
- What makes it hard: Opens the oldest revision first, nested document viewers, paged requirement tables.

### 3. ERP (`erp`)

- URL: <https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run>
- Login: required; each run brings its own username and password in `access`
- Holds: Your company's materials, stock, lead times and price conditions with validity periods and quantity scales.
- What makes it hard: SAP-style transaction codes, an F4 search popup, status codes, a short session timeout.

### 4. Webmail (Werkpost, `mail`)

- URL: <https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run>
- Login: required; each run brings its own username and password in `access`
- Holds: Your sales inbox, with the sales director's discount approval and the signing TAN.
- What makes it hard: Look-alike approvals for other tenders, superseded approvals, an archive folder, paging.

### Scout them yourself

Logins for every website, with the public data. Click around as much as you like. None of it is scored.

| Website | URL | Username | Password |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tender portal (Vergabeportal) | <https://atira-rfq-tender-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `uJC8-80QSb7rblI_k4tH` |
| Supplier portal (Lieferantenportal) | <https://atira-rfq-customer-portal.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `k2sBynnldp0mqU4MviqI` |
| ERP | <https://atira-rfq-erp.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `vuUcG2MsDEafLhoMjfS5` |
| Webmail (Werkpost) | <https://atira-rfq-mail.kyora.run> | `u_9c3cb06a5d21b197` | `ldPxYRdvI__aVKKqOWIy` |

## Public and private data

There are two datasets. The leaderboard uses the public one, on these websites. The final run uses a private dataset: the same jobs, bid rules and answer format, on different websites with other content and data. We pick the winners on three things, roughly in this order: performance on the private dataset, performance on the public dataset, and the elegance of the system.

- **Public dataset:** The leaderboard uses the public dataset (public-1), the websites and data you scout and test on. Each submission runs once on it. We don't publish the correct answer. Test runs and the scouting logins use it too.
- **Private dataset (the final run):** When the hackathon ends, we run each team's latest submission that passed review once by default, or best of three if the team opts in before the final run starts, on a private dataset. It is similar, not the same: the same jobs, the same bid rules and the same answer format, but different websites (other software, layout, navigation and site names), other content and data, and the information split differently across them. Your agent has to handle them as it finds them. That run weighs most when we pick the winners, so don't tune your agent to the public scenario.

## Bid rules

The brief states these rules in full. Together they define exactly one correct answer.

1. **Quantity:** The tender quantity, overridden by the latest clarification that changes that position.
2. **Requirement:** The position's requirement in the specification revision marked current.
3. **Material:** The active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification match exactly. If a position has none, the answer is no bid.
4. **Unit price:** The price condition valid on the scenario date, at the highest quantity scale reached, minus the approved discount, rounded half-up to the cent.
5. **Discount:** The most recent approval from the sales director for this exact tender; otherwise 0 %.
6. **Lead time:** The from-stock lead time when stock covers the quantity, otherwise the production lead time.
7. **Total:** The sum of quantity times unit price, rounded half-up to the cent.
8. **Decision:** Bid, with one entry per tender position; no bid with no positions and a total of 0 when a material is missing.
9. **Partial submission:** Full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
10. **Finding records:** The specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
11. **Agent requirement:** A language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
12. **Commercial clauses:** A tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
13. **Withdrawn answers:** A tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
14. **Scoped amendments:** After selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
15. **Shared stock:** Sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
16. **Conditional discount:** The latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yields 0 %.
17. **Units:** Tender and Q&A quantities use the position's stated unit. Convert Satz using the governing specification's pieces per set. Price scales, inventory, allocation weights and bid quantities all use final pieces. Carton rounding affects packaging cost only, never the bid quantity.
18. **Pricing breakdown:** Base_unit_price, surcharge_per_unit, packaging_per_unit and rebate_total are optional and earn independent credit. All monetary answers are net EUR. Base, surcharge and packaging are per piece; rebate_total is the credit for the whole position. Enter 0.00 for a known zero; blank means unanswered. Do not feed rounded per-piece breakdowns back into the final formula.
19. These calculation rules apply to both practice and private datasets. Missing calculation fields lose only their own points; signing an incomplete bid is supported.
20. **Technical derivation:** For a requirement marked nutzbarer Weg, apply its scoped amendments first, then add twice the per-end reserve from the revision-specific Technikfreigabe. Match the resulting nominal stroke to the ERP. Do not change the other attributes.
21. **Authority and time:** Resolve each key from the latest record no later than the scenario date, for the EXACT tender reference. Authorized subjects/senders (local part + bidder mailbox domain): Technikfreigabe/technik, Verpackungstarife/logistik, Terminfreigabe/logistik, Devisenfixing/finanzen, Rüstpools/kalkulation, Projektbonus/finanzen. A newer record replaces the older one; a failed quantity condition does not revive it. Unrelated references and future-dated records never apply.
22. **Currency:** The valid condition names its currency and FX key. Normalize its price unit, select the per-position quantity scale, then convert with EUR per currency unit and HALF_UP to cents. This converted base_unit_price is used in all subsequent calculations and approval thresholds.
23. **Packaging:** Q&A assigns the tariff key; ERP gives pieces per carton. Charge ceil(final pieces / carton size) cartons independently per position. Do not increase the bid quantity. Report packaging_per_unit in EUR, rounded HALF_UP; do not discount packaging.
24. **Delivery:** Q&A assigns a commitment key. Apply it only if its material matches and pooled final demand for that material is within its inclusive ceiling. Otherwise use shared-stock delivery. A commitment may differ by position even for the same material.
25. **Shared setup:** Q&A identifies pool members; ERP gives allocation mass (distinct from surcharge mass); the Rüstpools mail gives the one pool fee. Allocate by quantity × allocation mass using the cent-allocation rule in that mail. Add each allocation to that position's ordinary setup fee. Report surcharge_per_unit BEFORE discount, excluding packaging and bonus.
26. **Project bonus:** The finance mail gives marginal percentage bands. Compute the eligible undiscounted EUR goods total, apply each band only to its portion, round the aggregate credit HALF_UP to cents, then allocate proportionally to eligible line goods values using largest remainders in cents (ties: ascending position identifier). Report rebate_total as the allocated EUR CREDIT FOR THE ENTIRE POSITION, not per piece; enter zero for nonmembers. This bonus is independent of discount clauses.
27. **Final price:** Clause-discounted EUR base + clause-discounted mass surcharge + (ordinary setup + allocated shared setup + carton cost − allocated project bonus) / final piece quantity. Use unrounded per-piece components and round HALF_UP once at the end. Sum quantity × rounded final unit price for total_net. Rounded breakdown fields are reports, not inputs to that final formula.
28. **Metal indices:** Select the latest exact-reference Preisindizes message from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. If the code lists validity windows, use the rate whose inclusive window contains the scenario date, not the last rate listed.
29. **Scoring in bid cases:** Decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 minus any additional checks, correct total 5, arithmetic consistency 5. When present, the withdrawn Q&A quantity and date-selected metal-index checks earn 5 points each. Within each equally weighted position: material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%. Each field is independent; optional breakdown fields can be blank. No-bid scoring is unchanged.

## How a run works

Develop on your machine against the public websites with the scouting logins (`atira scout --env`), then test in the sandbox: `atira test-run` uploads your package, starts a test run and opens it live, or drop the package on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team). A test run lasts up to 2 hours on the public data and returns its score with the full breakdown. In the commands, `$ATIRA_TOKEN` holds your personal token (sign in with `atira login`, then `atira token`).

1. **Start.** The run issues a token, the task brief and fresh logins for every website.
2. **Read.** Your agent reads the brief, the rules and the answer format from the API.
3. **Work the websites.** It works through the 4 websites in a real browser and gathers the facts.
4. **Submit.** It enters the bid in the tender portal's configurator and signs it with a TAN from the webmail.
5. **Scored.** The answer is checked against the one correct answer; quality, cost and time are recorded.

### Develop locally

```sh
eval "$(atira scout --challenge rfq --env)"   # logins for the public websites
curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/challenges/rfq/scouting"   # the same, with the brief, as JSON
# run your agent on your machine, then once in the sandbox:
atira test-run ./my-agent --challenge rfq
```

`atira scout --env` exports the scouting logins as `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` (the shape a run gets), each website's URL, and `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, the brief and the answer format. It also points the free hosted models at `atira models proxy` on your computer, so your agent needs no model key; another provider takes your own. Nothing done there counts. With these logins, an answer entered on the tender portal is acknowledged but never counts. In a run, your agent reads the same at `GET /v1/runs/current` with the run token as `x-api-key`, and hands in one valid answer of up to 65,536 bytes; a malformed one returns its problems while the clock keeps running.

### Read the run

Inside a test or scored run, with the run token (`$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN`) in `RUN_TOKEN`:

```sh
curl "$ATIRA_API/v1/runs/current" -H "x-api-key: $RUN_TOKEN"
```

The response holds `brief` (the task in Markdown, with the rules), `access` (each website's `url` and `credentials`), `submission` (where the answer goes), `answer_schema`, `expires_at`, `llm_proxy_url` and `llm_providers`. Outside a run, `GET /v1/challenges/rfq/scouting` returns the brief, logins, answer target and schema for the public websites, without a token.

### In the sandbox

A test run and a scored run start your `run` command with these variables. `setup` runs before, with network but without them, for up to 5 minutes that don't count toward your time.

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `CHALLENGE_API_URL` | the platform API; the run is at /v1/runs/current |
| `CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN` | this run's token, sent as x-api-key |
| `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS` | the websites with this run's logins, as JSON |
| `LLM_PROXY_URL` | the model proxy with the run token in its path; bring your own provider key |
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/anthropic |
| `OPENAI_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/openai/v1 |
| `GOOGLE_GEMINI_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/google |
| `MISTRAL_SERVER_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/mistral |
| `TOGETHER_BASE_URL` | https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/together/v1 |
| `CLEF_BASE_URL`, `CLEF_API_KEY` | Clef through the proxy, https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/clef, with the run token as its key; free, no usage cap. |
| `QWEN_BASE_URL`, `QWEN_API_KEY` | Qwen through the proxy, https://atira-challenge.kyora.run/llm/run/$CHALLENGE_RUN_TOKEN/qwen/v1, with the run token as its key; free, no usage cap. |
| `CDP_URL` | the sandbox browser (Chrome DevTools Protocol), http://127.0.0.1:9222; with several, browser 1 |
| `CDP_URLS` | every browser's CDP URL in order, as a JSON array: one per browser asked for in agent.json, up to 4 |
| `BROWSER_COUNT` | how many browsers the sandbox started, 1 to 4 |
| `DISPLAY` | the desktop browser 1 runs on, :1 at 1280×800; browser n is on :n |
| `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `http_proxy`, `https_proxy` | the only way out: the platform and the websites (http://127.0.0.1:3128) |
| `NO_PROXY`, `no_proxy` | reached directly, so the browser's CDP stays local (localhost,127.0.0.1) |
| `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY` | Node's fetch uses the proxy (1) |

Every model call goes through the platform's metering proxy, which records its tokens and cost; the hosted models need no key, and any other provider takes the team's own. [The run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls) has the key and SDK settings for each provider.

## Unlimited Inference

We host Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Cloudflare's Clef for this hackathon, free and with no usage cap. On your laptop, `atira models proxy` gives you a URL and key (setup on [your team page](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/team#team-models)). In test and scored runs it's set up for you. Free for you. Each call still adds its simulated price to your run's cost, so the cost ranking stays fair.

### Qwen3.8-Flash-Next

#6 on the [Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index](https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/qwen3-8-flash-next) (open-weight, large models). Multimodal general-purpose LLM. Strong at reasoning, tool calls and reading pages and screenshots, with a 256k context, so it can plan, browse and write the answer.

- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 32 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
- **Simulated pricing:**
  - Input: $0.15 / M tokens
  - Cached input: $0.016 / M tokens
  - Cache writes: Free
  - Output: $0.47 / M tokens
- **Precision:** [NVFP4](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4) (NVIDIA's checkpoint)

Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.

```python
import os
from openai import OpenAI

qwen = OpenAI(
    base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"],
    api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
)
reply = qwen.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen",
    messages=[{
        "role": "user",
        "content": "Which button submits?",
    }],
)
```

### Cloudflare Clef

A multimodal decision model. Give it a state and up to 4 screenshots, then ask it questions: `choice` picks one of your options, `noul` gives the probability of yes, from 0 to 1, and `score` rates on a scale you set. See [Cloudflare's announcement](https://blog.cloudflare.com/clef-decision-models/) and [the benchmarks](https://clef-evals.workers-ai-mle.workers.dev). Worth a try for quick, low-stakes decisions, such as which link to open or whether a page is the right document, while the bigger model reads and reasons.

- **Limits:** No usage cap. Up to 16 calls per team at once, across all its runs; more wait in line.
- **Simulated pricing:**
  - Input: $0.24 / M tokens
  - Output: Not priced

Scales to zero when idle, but warm-up isn't counted toward a submission's time.

```sh
curl "$CLEF_BASE_URL/v1/decide" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CLEF_API_KEY" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "state": {"page": "Checkout returns 502"},
  "questions": {"next": {
    "type": "choice",
    "instructions": "What next?",
    "criteria": {
      "retry": "Retry the request",
      "report": "Report the error"}}}}'
```

In a run, `QWEN_BASE_URL` with `QWEN_API_KEY` and `CLEF_BASE_URL` with `CLEF_API_KEY` are set for you. On your machine, `atira models proxy` serves the same APIs on 127.0.0.1, so the same code works in both. Calls from your machine are free, recorded and never ranked. An idle model can take several minutes to wake on its first call, so use long timeouts.

```sh
atira login   # once per computer
atira models proxy   # keep it running; it prints:
export QWEN_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/qwen/v1
export QWEN_API_KEY=local
export CLEF_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8765/clef
export CLEF_API_KEY=local
```

content.text:
There's **no official GitHub repo** for the challenge. All the docs are on the Atira site as Markdown. The most complete version is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/llms-full.txt, which has every doc in one file, and the challenge page itself is https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq.md.

A GitHub search did turn up `DocMorphic/plite`, an "RFQ-to-bid agent for the Atira EHL challenge". It's another team's public repo, not something from Atira. Copying from it could get you flagged in Atira's automated code review, and it may not be correct anyway.

## The challenge: "From RFQ to bid"

You play a German maker of hydraulic cylinders bidding on a public tender. Your agent has to build **one correct, priced and signed bid** from information spread across four German-language websites:

| Site | What's there | What makes it hard |
|---|---|---|
| **Tender portal** (Vergabeportal) | The tender, the bill of quantities, a bidder Q&A that changes quantities, and the bid form where the answer goes | Cookie wall, flaky error pages, iframes, ZIP files, a deadline in another timezone |
| **Supplier portal** (Lieferantenportal) | The buyer's technical specification and its revisions | It opens the oldest revision first; nested document viewers; paged tables |
| **ERP** (SAP-style) | Materials, stock, lead times, price conditions with quantity scales | Transaction codes, an F4 search popup, short session timeouts |
| **Webmail** (Werkpost) | The sales director's discount approval and the TAN you sign the bid with | Look-alike and superseded approvals, an archive folder, paging |

**The core logic:**
1. Take each position's quantity from the tender, and apply the latest Q&A change that hasn't been withdrawn. Convert "Satz" (sets) into pieces.
2. Find the specification revision marked current, then apply any amendments that name it.
3. Find the active ERP material that matches bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification exactly. If any position has no match, the answer is **no bid**.
4. Unit price: the price condition valid on the scenario date, at the highest quantity scale the position reaches, minus the approved discount, rounded half-up to the cent.
5. Lead time: the from-stock time if stock covers the combined quantity for that material, otherwise the production time.
6. Enter the bid in the configurator and sign it with the TAN from the mail.

**On top of that come about 20 advanced rules** (rules 12–28 on the challenge page): discount groups, currency conversion, packaging per carton, shared setup-fee pools, a banded project bonus, metal-price indices, and conditional discounts with order-value thresholds. Most of the points for each position come from these breakdown fields.

**Scoring:** a correct bid decision is worth 5 points, the tender reference 5, the discount 5, the total 5, and arithmetic consistency 5. The positions share about 75 points. Within each position the split is material 20%, quantity 15%, base price 15%, then 10% each for surcharge, packaging, bonus, final price and delivery. Every field scores independently, so partial bids still earn points.

## Constraints
- A scored run gets **20 minutes**; a test run gets 2 hours. A late answer scores 0.
- The **winners are picked on a private dataset**: same rules, but different websites, layouts and data. So don't hardcode anything about the public sites.
- **A language model has to drive the navigation.** Helpers may parse a page, calculate or fill in forms. Crawlers, fixed scripts and values copied from the sites into your code get the submission rejected.
- You can use up to 4 browsers in parallel, and more than one agent.
- Models: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next and Clef are free with no cap, though each call still counts toward your run's cost ranking. Claude and other models need your own key and go through the metering proxy.
- The docs give no deadline. Ask the organizers.

The challenge page also lists scouting logins for all four sites, so you can look around by hand before building. Nothing you do with them counts.

content.text: So what is the technical hard part here? The browser use?

content.thinking:
The real difficulty isn't just browser use—it's navigating hostile UIs reliably with a weaker model under a time limit, correctly identifying the right evidence among decoys using time/authority rules, offloading the complex deterministic calculation to code rather than the LLM, and generalizing to unseen private sites without being able to script around them.

My recommended architecture: have the LLM handle navigation and structured fact extraction, then hand off to a deterministic Python rules engine for computation, running per-site agents in parallel with a fallback for partial submissions if time runs short. For browser interaction, I'd favor reading the accessibility tree/DOM text over screenshots, with explicit handling for iframes, ZIP/PDF downloads, popups, session timeouts, and TAN-based signing flows.

content.text:
Browser use is part of it, but it isn't the main difficulty. There are four hard problems, and they need different solutions.

## 1. Picking the right evidence (the real core)
The sites are full of deliberate decoys:
- The supplier portal opens the **oldest** spec revision first.
- The mailbox has look-alike approvals for other tenders, superseded approvals, future-dated mails and an archive folder.
- In the Q&A, later answers withdraw earlier ones, and amendments only apply to a specific revision.
- Records only count if they're for the exact tender reference, from an authorized sender and dated no later than the scenario date.

A model that finds a plausible-looking discount and stops will be confidently wrong. Your agent has to collect every candidate and then choose with explicit rules: latest date, exact reference, right sender, not withdrawn. Most of the points are lost here, not in clicking.

## 2. The calculation
Rules 12–28 add up to a small pricing engine: currency conversion, quantity scales, carton ceilings, setup pools split by mass, banded bonuses allocated by largest remainders, half-up rounding at specific steps, and conditional discount thresholds. **An LLM will get this wrong.** It should be plain Python with unit tests, fed structured facts the model extracted. The rules explicitly allow helpers that calculate. If you build only one deterministic piece, build this one.

## 3. Generalizing to the private dataset
The final run uses different software, layouts, navigation and site names, with the information split differently. That rules out anything tuned to the public sites: no selectors, no click paths, no "the ERP uses transaction code X". The agent has to read whatever page it lands on and decide. You also can't solve this by crawling everything, because rule 11 forbids that.

## 4. Browser robustness within 20 minutes
This is the browser-use part: cookie walls, flaky error pages, iframes, ZIP and PDF downloads, F4 search popups, short ERP session timeouts that log you out, and paging. With Qwen-Flash as the free model, every step is cheap but takes some time. A serial agent that reads four sites one after another will run out of time. The usual fixes are:
- Give the model a compact page view (text plus a numbered list of clickable elements) instead of raw HTML or only screenshots.
- Write generic helpers for re-login, iframe flattening and file download and parsing. These are allowed.
- Use 4 browsers, with one sub-agent per site running in parallel.

## The shape that works
```
Planner (LLM) reads the brief
  → 4 site agents in parallel (LLM navigates, extracts JSON facts with sources and dates)
  → resolver (code): picks the latest valid record per rule
  → pricing engine (code, unit-tested)
  → submit agent (LLM): fills the form, gets the TAN from the mail, signs
```
Also submit a partial bid before the deadline. Omitted positions just get no points, and everything else still scores.

Order of difficulty: evidence selection, then generalizing to new sites, then the calculation (hard to write, easy to test), then browser mechanics (fiddly but solvable with generic helpers).

My suggestion for where to start: scout the four sites by hand for 20 minutes to see where the decoys are, then build the pricing engine and its tests first. It's the one part you can fully check offline.

Prepare one net EUR bid for Stadt Buchenstadt, Verkehrsbetriebe: Lieferung von Hydraulikzylinder für Werkstatt-Hebeanlagen (VG-2027-7093). The scenario date is 2027-01-25T09:00:00Z; the tender deadline is 2027-02-12T11:00:00Z.

Collect the tender and its clarifications from the tender portal (Vergabeportal, `tender-portal`), the technical specification from the buyer's supplier portal (Lieferantenportal, `customer-portal`), materials and prices from the internal ERP (`erp`), and discount approvals from the sales mailbox in the webmail (Werkpost, `mail`). The websites are in German; obsolete documents and unrelated records are present.

## Rules

1. Quantity: start with the original tender quantity. For each position, use the quantity in the latest dated clarification that changes that position, if any.
2. Requirement: use the requirement referenced by the position in the specification revision marked current. Superseded revisions do not apply.
3. Material: select an active ERP material whose bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification all exactly equal that requirement. Blocked materials do not qualify. If any position has no matching active material, submit no_bid.
4. Unit price: use the material's price condition valid on the scenario date, including both validity endpoints. Choose the scale with the highest minimum quantity no greater than the final quantity. Apply the approved discount to that scale price and round the resulting unit price half up to the nearest cent.
5. Discount: use the most recent message from the sales director (leitung@ followed by the bidder's mailbox domain) that approves a discount for this exact tender reference. Approvals for other references and messages from other senders do not apply. If there is no approval, use zero percent.
6. Lead time: use the delivery-from-stock lead time in weeks when stock covers the final quantity; otherwise use the production lead time in weeks.
7. Total: sum each final quantity multiplied by its rounded discounted unit price, then round the total net amount half up to the nearest cent.
8. Decision: submit bid with one entry per tender position, identified by its position number, and currency EUR. If any active matching material is missing, submit no_bid with no positions and a total of zero.


## Additional rules

These refine rules 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 and 7 above. Every submitted quantity is in pieces.

- Partial submission: full credit requires every position, but the bid form lets you explicitly omit unfinished positions (Position auslassen / Teilpunkte). They receive no position points; completed positions retain their independent credit. Review lists the omitted position numbers. You must still sign and submit a bid; saving alone is not scored. A missing active material still calls for no_bid for full correctness; omission is a way to submit incomplete work, not a replacement decision rule.
- Finding records: the specification/data sheet names a Kataloggruppe for each requirement. Search the ERP for that group, then compare candidate attributes. Empty or over-broad searches do not list the catalogue; narrow to at most 20 results. Mail search combines words with AND: use the tender reference plus a subject/topic. Read the appropriate inbox/archive results. Opened pages and selected result sets may be extracted by helpers. Sites and positions can be investigated in parallel; no shared request quota or mandatory site order applies.
- Agent requirement: a language model must choose navigation targets, searches and relevant documents from observations at runtime and make the important decisions. Helpers may extract a selected page, parse a selected document, paginate a model-selected result set, calculate, validate, retry and fill forms. They must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation. Multiple agents and parallel browser sessions are allowed.
- Commercial clauses: a tender Q&A answer may assign a position to a Konditionsgruppe. Resolve that key in the latest Konditionsregeln message for the exact reference from kalkulation@ plus the bidder mailbox domain. Its prose determines whether discount applies to base only, base plus mass surcharge, or neither; setup fees are always excluded. A group overrides the default rule, even when two positions select the same material. The separately reported surcharge is always BEFORE any discount. Positions without a group use the default base-only rule. The order-level approved percentage and its threshold calculation do not change.
- Withdrawn answers: a tender Q&A answer may withdraw (zurückziehen) an earlier answer by its number. Ignore the withdrawn answer's quantity change; the latest remaining change applies, otherwise the tender quantity.
- Scoped amendments: after selecting the governing full specification revision, read the tender Q&A for technical amendments naming that revision and requirement. Apply only the named attributes; all others are inherited. The latest dated applicable amendment wins per attribute. Amendments to other revisions do not apply.
- Shared stock: sum final quantities of all positions selecting the same material. Stock must cover that entire sum for every such position to use stock delivery; otherwise all use production delivery. No partial stock allocation. Price scales remain per position, not per material sum.
- Conditional discount: the latest exact-reference director approval may require a minimum undiscounted net order value. Compute that value from final quantities and valid per-position scale prices before any discount and excluding mass surcharges and setup fees, rounded half up to cents. The threshold is inclusive. If it fails, use 0 %, without falling back to older approvals. For no_bid a conditional approval yie

The practical approach is to extract all candidate facts with their metadata and apply the appropriate filter/tie-break per type.

I should let extraction stay mechanical rather than having the LLM pick, then verify correctness through the per-field score breakdown from test runs since that's the only real ground truth. content.text:
You don't judge it by gut feeling: **the brief defines it exactly.** It says the rules "together define exactly one correct answer". Every fact has a filter (which records count at all) and a tie-break (which of the remaining ones wins). The decoys are built to break one of those, such as the wrong tender reference, the wrong sender, a superseded revision or a later date.

## Two anchors from the brief
The run's brief gives you both. For the public scenario:
- **Tender reference:** `VG-2027-7093`
- **Scenario date:** `2027-01-25T09:00:00Z`

Almost every rule filters on these two values: the exact reference and "no later than the scenario date".

## The selection rule for each fact

| Fact | Counts only if… | Winner if several |
|---|---|---|
| **Quantity** | It comes from a Q&A clarification that changes this position and hasn't been withdrawn (*zurückziehen*) | The latest dated one; otherwise the tender quantity |
| **Spec requirement** | It's in the revision marked **current**, not a superseded one | Then apply the Q&A amendments that name that revision and attribute; the latest wins per attribute |
| **Material** | It's active (not blocked) and bore, stroke, pressure, mounting and certification are **all exactly equal** | Exactly one should match; none means no bid |
| **Price condition** | It's valid on the scenario date, with both endpoints included | The scale with the highest minimum quantity that is ≤ the final quantity |
| **Discount** | Sender is `leitung@<bidder domain>`, it's for the **exact** reference and dated ≤ the scenario date | The most recent; if its minimum-order condition fails, use **0%** and don't fall back to an older approval |
| **Other mails** (Konditionsregeln, Technikfreigabe, Rüstpools, …) | The subject comes from its authorized sender (`kalkulation@`, `technik@`, `logistik@`, `finanzen@`), with the exact reference and a date ≤ the scenario date | The latest |

The trap sits in the second column: a perfectly real approval that's for `VG-2027-7039`, from `vertrieb@` instead of `leitung@`, or dated next week.

## How to build it
**Have the model extract and have code decide.** Don't ask the LLM "what's the discount?". Ask it to pull every candidate it sees into structured records:
```json
{"type": "discount_approval", "percent": 4.5, "sender": "leitung@linden-hydraulik.de",
 "reference": "VG-2027-7093", "date": "2027-01-20", "min_order_value": 25000,
 "folder": "archive", "source_url": "..."}
```
Then a deterministic resolver applies the filters and tie-breaks above. That's allowed, because helpers may "calculate and validate". It also makes errors debuggable: you can see whether the decoy was never extracted or was extracted but filtered wrongly.

You can code this resolver against the rules because the private dataset uses the **same rules**. What you can't hardcode is anything about the sites themselves: names, layouts or values.

The model's actual job is then to **find all the candidates**. It has to look in the archive folder as well as the inbox, page through results, and open the current spec revision instead of the first one it sees.

## How you check it
The correct answer is never published, so you have two ways to check:
1. **Scout by hand.** Log in to the four sites with the scouting credentials, work out the public-1 bid yourself and write it down as your expected answer. Doing it once takes about an hour, and you'll see every trap.
2. **Use test runs.** `atira test-run` returns the score broken down by field (material, quantity, base price and so on). A field that comes back wrong tells you which selection rule failed.

I can save the full brief and the 29 rules into the repo, which gives you the spec to build the resolver from.

content.thinking:
I need to be careful here - retrieval should be model-directed rather than an autonomous crawler grabbing everything indiscriminately, per the rules. It's also iterative rather than one-shot: the catalog group from the spec feeds into the ERP search, while the tender reference and topic drive the mail search, with Q&A results guiding further steps.

Resolver output can surface missing facts that trigger another retrieval pass, forming a loop. Resolver and calc logic might be merged, and there should be a validation step checking completeness. Submission needs the TAN pulled from mail at the right moment, likely after a signing request is issued, meaning the submit agent needs mail access again — plus I should account for partial submission fallback and time budget constraints.

There's tension in the rules: the model must make the important decisions, like choosing relevant documents, but if deterministic code decides everything, that risks violating the spirit of model-led decision-making. A hybrid approach resolves this better — the LLM proposes which documents matter and why, code cross-validates against rules, and disagreements trigger a re-look. That's safer for review and more robust overall, which should score well on elegance too. Now I want to sketch a refined, concise diagram of this flow.

content.text:
Yes, that's the right shape. Before you build it, I'd change three things, and one of them is about the rules.

## 1. Retrieval has to be model-directed, not "gather everything"
Rule 11 is explicit. Helpers "must not autonomously discover and traverse the websites to assemble the complete task evidence before model-directed investigation". If your retrieval layer is a crawler that dumps every page into JSON, the automated review rejects it.

The way to stay allowed: **the LLM decides** which page to open, what to search for and which document matters. Helpers then do the mechanical work: extract the page it picked, parse a PDF or ZIP it opened, page through a result list it chose. The data still ends up as JSON. The difference is who chose to look there.

## 2. It's a loop, not a pipeline
Many facts depend on other facts:
- the spec gives a **Kataloggruppe**, which tells you what to search for in the ERP;
- the Q&A assigns a **Konditionsgruppe** or tariff key, which tells you which mail to look up;
- the tender reference plus a topic becomes the **mail search** (search terms are ANDed).

So after the first pass, the resolver should report **what's still missing or ambiguous**, for example "position 3: no Konditionsregeln mail found yet" or "two approvals with the same date". That goes back to retrieval as a targeted task. You loop until everything is complete or time runs short.

## 3. Let the model decide, and let code check it
Rule 11 also says the model must "make the important decisions". If deterministic code silently picks every record, a reviewer could argue the system isn't agentic. Robustness also improves if you make it two-sided:
- **The LLM proposes:** "the current revision is C, the valid approval is mail #12, because …"
- **The code verifies** the proposal against the filters (exact reference, sender, date ≤ scenario date, not withdrawn).
- **If they disagree,** the system goes back and looks again instead of guessing.

That passes review, catches extraction mistakes, and fits the "elegance of the system" criterion.

## Refined architecture
```
            ┌──────────── missing / ambiguous facts ────────────┐
            ▼                                                   │
Planner (LLM) ──▶ Site agents ×4 (LLM navigates; helpers extract)
                     │  candidate records as JSON, with sources │
                     ▼                                          │
              Resolver: LLM proposes + code verifies against rules ┘
                     │  one fact per slot, or "missing"
                     ▼
              Pricing engine (pure Python, unit-tested)
                     │  bid JSON + self-checks (sums, rounding)
                     ▼
              Submit agent (LLM): fill the configurator → ask for signing
                     → get the TAN from the mail → sign
```

## Two operational points
- **The TAN probably arrives only when you request signing**, so the submit agent needs the mail inbox again at the very end. Reserve 3–4 minutes for this step.
- **Use a time watchdog.** At about 15 minutes, stop retrieving, omit the unfinished positions (*Position auslassen*) and sign what you have. A partial bid scores, and a late one scores 0.

A good first step is the record schema: one JSON type per fact type (quantity change, spec revision, material, price condition, approval, clause mail). Retrieval, resolver and pricing engine all depend on it, so it's the contract that lets your team work on the parts in parallel. I can draft that schema plus the pricing engine skeleton in `my-agent/`.

=================== docs/fair-play.md
# Fair play

**Rules at a glance**

You submit an agentic system: one agent or several. In the sandbox it does the whole job on its own: finds what it needs on the four websites, works out the bid and submits it. Nobody helps it during a run.

**Not allowed**

- **Hardcoding:** copying values from the websites into your package (prices, material numbers, totals, discounts, logins, TANs), including in prompts and notes, also as defaults or fallbacks. Using what the task brief tells every team, like the sales director's mailbox, is fine.
- **Pre-solving:** working out the answer yourself, or having an AI assistant do it, and putting the result in your package. Exploring the sites with an assistant is fine.
- **Scripts instead of agents:** a fixed click path, or a crawler that grabs everything for one model call. A model has to choose where to go, what to search for and what matters.
- **Outside help during a run:** contacting anything besides our platform and the four websites, calling a model other than through our proxy (your own API keys work through it), running a model inside the sandbox, or starting your own browsers (use the up to 4 provided). Setup may install dependencies.

**How it's checked:** an AI reviewer reads every submitted package before its scored run. Unclear cases are flagged and stay off the leaderboard until an organizer has looked. The final runs on websites and data your system hasn't seen.

The details follow.

## Allowed

- Any agent design; the free hosted models, or any provider and model with your own key, through the proxy; any
  amount of tokens.
  The proxy forwards your calls unchanged and measures them: reported usage is metered at the published model
  prices, and an upstream-reported USD cost takes precedence. See [the run contract](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#llm-calls)
  for SDK configuration.
- Keeping your model key as a [team secret](https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md#team-secrets) rather than in your package.
- Your own code, prompts and tools; open-source libraries installed during setup.
- Using what you learned with the scouting logins and in test runs about how the websites work.

I'm thinking the core principle is that the model decides where to look and what matters based on observation, while code handles the mechanical execution and verification — testable by asking whether the code would still work on a differently-structured site, and whether it's deciding or merely acting on a decision. I want to lay out a table distinguishing LLM tasks, code tasks, and gray-zone cases like a login helper, where finding the form is judgment but filling credentials is mechanical.

I'm also sketching litmus tests: removing the LLM to see if progress still happens, swapping the website to see if the code still makes sense, and checking who chose the input the code acts on — any hardcoded site-specific selectors should be flagged as scripted shortcuts that would break on a private dataset. Since the reviewer is an AI reading the code, I want the structure itself to make clear that the agent loop is driving things, with a concrete example of a tool interface exposing actions like opening pages, clicking, typing, searching, reading, paginating, and proposing records, while code only validates, computes, and fills forms.

content.text:
Atira's fair-play doc draws the line itself:

> *"A model decides where to go on the websites, finds the information and makes the decisions. Code can help it (browser control, parsing, arithmetic, checks, reading a page or document the model chose, paging through results it asked for)… Rejected: a fixed script that clicks through known pages with the model unused or only as a fallback, and a crawler that collects the websites and hands everything to the model at the end."*

In short: **the model decides *where* to go and *what matters*. Code does the *how* (mechanics) and the *math* (calculations and checks).**

## Who does what

| Task | LLM | Code |
|---|---|---|
| Which site, menu, link or tab to open next | ✅ | |
| What to type into a search ("VG-2027-7093 Rabatt") | ✅ | |
| Which search result or document is relevant | ✅ | |
| "This is revision C; it's marked current" | ✅ | ✅ checks it |
| Clicking, typing, waiting, retrying a flaky page | | ✅ |
| Logging in with the run's credentials, re-logging after a timeout | | ✅ (generic) |
| Dismissing cookie walls and popups | | ✅ (generic) |
| Turning a page the model picked into clean text or a table | | ✅ |
| Unzipping and parsing a PDF the model opened | | ✅ |
| Paging through a result list the model searched for | | ✅ (explicitly allowed) |
| Pulling facts out of a page into JSON | ✅ | ✅ validates the schema |
| Choosing which record wins | ✅ proposes | ✅ verifies against the rules |
| Price, rounding, allocation, totals | | ✅ |
| Filling the bid form from the computed JSON | | ✅ (filling forms is allowed) |
| Finding the TAN mail and reading the TAN | ✅ | |

## Four tests to apply to any piece of code
1. **Take the LLM out.** Can the code still get somewhere on public-1? If so, it's a script, and the review rejects it.
2. **Swap in a different website.** Does the code still make sense? `page.click("#tx-me23n")` doesn't, which makes it a fixed click path, and it breaks on the private dataset. `click(element_id_the_model_chose)` does.
3. **Who chose this input?** Code may act only on targets the model picked. "Extract this page" is fine; "visit every page under /docs" isn't.
4. **Is any value from the sites in the package?** No prices, material numbers, tender references or TANs anywhere, including prompts, defaults and fallbacks. Rules the brief states, like `leitung@` being the director's mailbox, are fine.

## In code: the LLM gets tools
In practice the line is your tool interface. The LLM runs a loop and calls tools; each tool is dumb, generic code:

```python
TOOLS = {
  # navigation (the model chooses the target)
  "open":        open_link,        # element id or URL the model picked
  "click":       click_element,
  "type":        type_into,
  "search":      run_search,       # the model writes the query
  "next_page":   next_result_page, # pages through the list it asked for
  # reading (helpers extract what the model selected)
  "read_page":   extract_page_text,     # text + numbered clickable elements
  "open_doc":    parse_document,        # PDF/ZIP → text
  # output
  "record_fact": save_candidate,        # model writes a JSON record + source
  "propose":     propose_slot,          # "approval = mail #12, because …"
}
# code-only, after the loop:
verified = resolver.check(proposals, candidates, brief)   # rules 1–28 as filters
bid      = pricing.compute(verified)                     # pure math
```

The site agents never run code paths they didn't choose. The resolver and the pricing engine never touch the browser.

## The gray zones, and how I'd handle them
- **Login and cookie helpers:** fine, as long as they're generic. Detect a password field rather than a hardcoded selector.
- **A tool that extracts every row of a table:** fine if the model opened that table. It's a crawler only if code decides to go and open all the tables.
- **The resolver choosing the winning record:** keep the model as the one who proposes it. That satisfies "the model makes the decisions", and the code check catches the model's mistakes.
- **Prompts that teach site knowledge**, like "the ERP uses F4 search": avoid them. The private sites use different software, so give general guidance ("look for a search or lookup dialog") instead.

The reviewer is an AI that reads your whole package. A clear tool layer with the agent loop visibly in charge is the easiest design for it to pass. Don't add notes asking the reviewer to approve the code: they don't count as evidence, and instructions that try to steer the verdict count against you.

content.text:
**It works, and it's allowed.** The sandbox has Node 24. `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` already points at Atira's proxy, and your Anthropic key can be stored as a team secret. The setup step has network access, so it can `npm install` Claude Code and a Playwright MCP server, which can attach to the provided browsers over CDP. The docs even mention driving Claude's computer-use tool. A model makes every decision, so the "must be agentic" rule is easily met.

So `agent.json` would roughly be: setup installs `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` and `@playwright/mcp`, and run calls `claude -p "<brief + rules>"` with the browser MCP. That's maybe 30 lines of glue.

But "no code" runs into four problems:

**1. Twenty minutes is tight for one agent.** Claude Code with a browser MCP is slow per step: each page snapshot is thousands of tokens, and Claude thinks before every click. Four sites, a dozen documents, paging, the archive folder, then signing: a single serial agent will probably run out of time. Subagents with one browser each help, but you still have to set that up.

**2. The arithmetic.** Rules 12–28 include currency conversion, carton ceilings, setup costs allocated by mass, banded bonuses with largest-remainder cent allocation, and rounding at exact steps. Claude would write Python on the fly to do it, a fresh version in every run. Each version can have a slightly different bug, and every pricing field is scored separately.

**3. Variance on the run that counts.** The winner is decided by one run, or the best of three, on unseen sites. A free-form agent sometimes skips the archive folder, or stops at the first plausible discount mail. You can't unit-test a prompt the way you can test a resolver.

**4. Context and cost.** Twenty minutes of browser snapshots fills the context window, and compaction can drop exactly the date or sender detail you need. Cost is only the tiebreaker after quality, so this matters less, but Claude costs many times more than the free Qwen.

**On the plus side,** Claude is far better than Qwen-Flash at messy German business UIs, and quality ranks before cost. A strong model with light structure may well beat a cheap model with heavy structure.

## What I'd actually do
Start with Claude driving the browser, then add code only where test runs show failures:

1. **Day 1, about 2 hours:** a pure Claude Code (or Agent SDK) agent with a browser MCP and the rules in its prompt. Run `atira test-run` and read the per-field score breakdown. This gives you a working baseline fast.
2. **Then add a little code where it fails:**
   - **A pricing tool:** a tested Python function that Claude calls with the facts it found, instead of doing the math itself. This is almost certainly needed.
   - **A `record_fact` tool** that saves candidates to a JSON file, so facts survive context compaction.
   - **A verifier** that checks Claude's chosen records against the filters (exact reference, sender, date).
   - **Subagents per site** if the run takes too long.

Claude still steers the browser the whole way. The code is just the parts that have to be exact every time. Overall that's a few hundred lines of glue and pricing code. You do need an Anthropic API key with credit for test runs.

I can set up the baseline in `my-agent/`: `agent.json`, the Claude Code invocation with Playwright MCP over CDP, and a prompt built from the brief.
